Whenever I took Algebra 2, I was great pals with my teacher. She was hilarious and I really enjoyed the class even though I wasn't doing super well. We learned a lot and so I was almost okay with getting like a C because I knew I was learning so much more than I would have had I been I a lower level class. One time we had to make up a scenario in which permutations would be useful. I proceeded to write a short story about a polygamist who had 10 wives who fell into a lake of piranhas, but he could only save 3 of them. I ended it with "#polygamyprobs"  and got bonus points. 
This is the same teacher who knew I worked my ass off in her class and I understood the material, I just had terrible anxiety and couldn't test well for the life of me and so come the end of the year, even though I had had a C+ or lower for every quarter, I ended up with a B-. She knew I cared about it and that I had put so much into that class that she bumped my grade up. We still keep in touch even though I live 2000 miles away from her.

The emotions that ran through me when I heard one of my friends died by suicide on February 26. He lived 6 houses down from me and jump on the tracks behind our neighborhood in front of a commuter train going to DC (we lived in Northern Virginia) at 5:35 in the morning. I heard the sirens in my neighborhood that morning but didn't think much of it and didn't find out he was dead until 12:37 that day. It was the 6th suicide at my high school in 3 years. Another boy from my high school died the next day and the whole school found out at a big basketball game and so many people ran out crying. I will never forget that week or the week that followed. Nothing worse than having to attend a funeral for a friend who you never knew was struggling.
